original_question: For a graph G with maximum degree Delta(G), is the list packing number always at most Delta(G) + 1? In other words, must chi*_l(G) <= Delta(G) + 1 hold for every graph G?
target_in_paper: Section 2, under “Upper bound by a function of maximum degree,” Problem 2.5 of arXiv:2411.10046. This is the workshop-paper restatement of the main bounded-degree list-packing question from the cited paper [5], namely Conjecture 3(i) in Section 1 of List packing number of bounded degree graphs.
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the correct parameter (maximum degree Δ(G)), the correct invariant (the list packing number χ^*_ℓ(G)), the correct universal quantifier (for every graph G), and the exact inequality asked in the paper, χ^*_ℓ(G) ≤ Δ(G) + 1. It is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of Problem 2.5.
missing_details: The draft does not define χ^*_ℓ(G). In the paper, χ^*_ℓ(G) is the least integer k such that every k-list-assignment L of G admits an L-packing of size k.
It omits the definition of a k-list-assignment: a function L: V(G) → 2^N with |L(v)| = k for every vertex v.
It omits the definition of an L-colouring and properness: a colouring c with c(v) ∈ L(v) for all v, and c(u) ≠ c(v) for every edge uv.
It omits the definition of disjointness for the packed colourings: if c1, ..., ck are the colourings, then ci(v) ≠ cj(v) for every vertex v and all i ≠ j.
It does not explicitly say that no extra hypotheses are imposed: the question is over all graphs, not only planar, bipartite, connected, regular, or bounded-order graphs.
It does not mention that the paper frames this as the central maximum-degree upper-bound problem for list packing, i.e. a Brooks-type analogue for χ^*_ℓ.
There are no ambient ring/field, homogeneity, nilpotency, or 'for sufficiently large' conditions in this problem; the hidden content is entirely in the graph-theoretic definitions above.
refined_question: Let G be a graph. For an integer k, a k-list-assignment of G is a function L: V(G) → 2^N such that |L(v)| = k for every v ∈ V(G). An L-colouring c of G is proper if c(v) ∈ L(v) for all v and c(u) ≠ c(v) whenever uv ∈ E(G). A collection c1, ..., ck of proper L-colourings is pairwise disjoint if ci(v) ≠ cj(v) for every v ∈ V(G) and all i ≠ j. Define the list packing number χ^*_ℓ(G) to be the least integer k such that every k-list-assignment L of G admits k pairwise-disjoint proper L-colourings. Is it true that χ^*_ℓ(G) ≤ Δ(G) + 1 for every graph G?
justification: Problem 2.5 in Section 2 of arXiv:2411.10046 is exactly the maximum-degree question your draft is aiming at, and the notation needed to read it self-containedly is defined immediately beforehand in the same section. The cited bounded-degree paper [5] confirms that this is not a side variant but the authors’ main maximum-degree conjecture for list packing, with small-degree evidence and a proved fractional relaxation nearby. So the faithful refinement is to keep your inequality unchanged and add only the missing definitions of k-list-assignment, proper L-colouring, disjointness, and χ^*_ℓ(G).
